The '''2024 Copa Sudamericana final''' was the final match which decided the winner of the [[2024 Copa Sudamericana]]. This was the 23rd edition of the [[Copa Sudamericana]], the second-tier South American continental club [[Association football|football]] tournament organized by [[CONMEBOL]].

The match was played by Argentine club [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing]] and Brazilian side [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] on 23 November 2024 at the [[Estadio General Pablo Rojas]] in [[Asunción]], Paraguay.<ref name=Venue>{{cite web |url=https://www.directvsports.com/futbol/Alejandro-Dominguez-confirmo-que-la-final-de-la-Sudamericana-se-juega-en-la-Nueva-Olla-20241007-0044.html |title=Alejandro Domínguez confirmó que la final de la Sudamericana se jugará en La Nueva Olla |trans-title=Alejandro Domínguez confirmed that the Sudamericana final will be played at La Nueva Olla |publisher=[[DSports]] |language=es |date=7 October 2024 |access-date=23 October 2024}}</ref>

Racing defeated Cruzeiro 3–1 in the match to win their first Copa Sudamericana title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/racing-club-levanta-la-conmebol-sudamericana-2024/ |title=Racing Club levanta la CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2024 |trans-title=Racing Club lift the 2024 CONMEBOL Sudamericana |language=es |publisher=CONMEBOL |date=23 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com/articles/soccer/argentinas-racing-wins-its-first-copa-sudamericana-championship-by-beating-brazils-cruzeiro-31 |title=Argentina's Racing wins its first Copa Sudamericana championship by beating Brazil's Cruzeiro 3-1 |publisher=[[Fox Sports]] |date=23 November 2024 |access-date=23 November 2024}}</ref> This was their first international title since the [[1988 Supercopa Libertadores]].

As winners of the 2024 Copa Sudamericana, Racing earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2024 Copa Libertadores]] in the [[2025 Recopa Sudamericana]]. They also automatically qualified for the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]] group stage.

== Venue ==
[[File:Racing Club vs. Cruzeiro - CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2024.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|A giant screen was set up on the field at [[El Cilindro]] in Avellaneda for Racing fans who could not travel to Paraguay to watch the match.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 November 2024 |title=Como en el 2001: Racing volvió a llenar dos canchas el mismo día |trans-title=Just like in 2001: Racing filled up two stadiums on the same day again |url=https://www.tycsports.com/racing-club/como-en-2001-racing-vuelve-a-llenar-dos-canchas-el-mismo-dia-id620860.html |access-date=23 December 2024 |publisher=[[TyC Sports]]|website=www.tycsports.com |language=es}}</ref>]]
On 10 April 2024, CONMEBOL announced the cities selected to host the finals of the [[2024 Copa Sudamericana|2024]] and [[2025 Copa Sudamericana]] editions, with [[Asunción]] being appointed for the 2024 final at a stadium to be confirmed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/asuncion-y-santa-cruz-sedes-confirmadas-para-finales-de-la-conmebol-sudamericana/ |title=¡Asunción y Santa Cruz recibirán a la Gran Conquista! |trans-title=Asunción and Santa Cruz will host the Great Conquest! |publisher=CONMEBOL |language=es |date=10 April 2024 |access-date=10 April 2024}}</ref> Shortly afterwards, the confederation confirmed that it would invest funds on improvements to the infrastructure of stadiums that had been put forward as potential hosts for the finals of the [[2024 Copa Libertadores final|Copa Libertadores]] and the Copa Sudamericana, which in the latter's case were [[Estadio Defensores del Chaco]], [[Estadio General Pablo Rojas]] (also known as "''La Nueva Olla''"), [[Estadio Osvaldo Domínguez Dibb]], and [[Estadio Tigo La Huerta|Estadio La Huerta]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://d10.ultimahora.com/conmebol-remozara-estadios-para-finales-de-la-copa-libertadores-y-la-sudamericana |title=Conmebol remozará estadios para finales de la Copa Libertadores y la Sudamericana |trans-title=CONMEBOL will refurbish stadiums for Copa Libertadores and Sudamericana finals |publisher=D10 |language=es |date=18 April 2024 |access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref>

On 7 October 2024, CONMEBOL president [[Alejandro Domínguez (football executive)|Alejandro Domínguez]] confirmed Estadio General Pablo Rojas as the venue for the final match. This was the second Copa Sudamericana final played at the stadium, after the [[2019 Copa Sudamericana final|2019 one]] in which Ecuadorian side [[Independiente del Valle]] defeated [[Club Atlético Colón|Colón]] from Argentina.<ref name=Venue/>

==Format==
The final was played as a single match at a pre-selected venue, with the higher-seeded team designated as the "home" team for administrative purposes. If scores were level after full time, 30 minutes of extra time would be played. If still tied after extra time, a penalty shoot-out would be used to determine the winners.<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=https://cdn.conmebol.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Manual-de-Clubes-CS-2024-ESP-Digital.pdf|title=Manual de Clubes CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2024|publisher=CONMEBOL|access-date=25 October 2024}}</ref>
